title: The Memory Model, Escape Analysis, and Performance

questions.prompt: What decides whether a value goes on the stack or the heap in Go?

options.text: The programmer, with explicit new/heap keywords

questions.explanation: Escape analysis places values that don't outlive their function on the stack, and promotes escaping values to the heap; observe it with -gcflags=-m.

questions.prompt: Is it safe to return a pointer to a local variable in Go?

options.text: Yes — escape analysis moves the value to the heap so it stays valid
No — it produces a dangling pointer, like in C

questions.explanation: Because the value's reference outlives the function, escape analysis allocates it on the heap and the GC keeps it alive — no dangling pointer.

questions.prompt: The memory model guarantees one goroutine sees another's writes only when synchronization establishes a ____-before relationship.
questions.explanation: Happens-before, established by channels, mutexes, sync.Once, WaitGroup, and atomics, is what makes concurrent visibility well-defined; otherwise it's a data race.

questions.prompt: What is the golden rule before optimizing Go code?

options.text: Measure first — profile and benchmark to find the real hotspots

questions.explanation: Most bottlenecks aren't where you'd guess; clarity is the default and you optimize only proven hotspots identified by benchmarks and profiles.

questions.prompt: Which statements about Go's garbage collector and memory are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: The GC is a concurrent, low-latency mark-and-sweep collector
GOGC (default 100) controls heap growth between collections
You must manually free heap memory

questions.explanation: Go's GC is concurrent mark-and-sweep, GOGC tunes it, and preallocation cuts allocations. You never manually free — the GC does it.

questions.prompt: Match each performance lever to its effect.
questions.explanation: Preallocation and Builder cut allocations, sync.Pool reuses objects at proven hotspots, and -gcflags=-m reveals what escapes.
